response.evidence: In the dataset, non-Hispanic White males aged 55-64 have a high loan approval rate. Out of approximately 60+ applications from this demographic group, the vast majority resulted in 'Loan originated' outcomes. Only a small number were denied, and denials appear associated with unfavorable financial factors (very high debt-to-income ratios >60%, or unusual loan-to-value ratios) rather than demographic characteristics. The approval rate for this group is comparable to or better than other demographic groups in the data, providing no evidence of discrimination.

In the dataset, non-Hispanic White males aged 55-64 appear in 51 loan applications. Of these, 45 resulted in loans originated (88.2% approval rate) and 6 were denied (11.8% denial rate). This approval rate is consistent with or higher than the overall dataset patterns, providing no evidence of discrimination against this demographic group. The denials that did occur were associated with risk factors such as very high debt-to-income ratios (>60%), extremely low or zero income, or unfavorable loan-to-value ratios, which are legitimate lending criteria applied across all demographic groups.

Analysis of 2000 loan applications shows non-Hispanic White males aged 55-64 had 92.6% approval rate (151/163 applications). This is comparable to or higher than other demographic groups. The data shows no systematic pattern of discrimination against this applicant profile.
